title: Compact-open currying for a locally compact source
statement: Let $A,K,Z$ be topological spaces, with $K$ locally compact, meaning that every point has a neighborhood basis of compact sets. Give $A\times K$ its product topology and $\operatorname{Cont}(K,Z)$ the compact-open topology generated by $[L,U]=\{h:h(L)\subseteq U\}$ for compact $L\subseteq K$ and open $U\subseteq Z$. Every continuous $h:A\times K\to Z$ has a continuous transpose $h^\sharp:A\to\operatorname{Cont}(K,Z)$, $h^\sharp(a)(k)=h(a,k)$. Every continuous $g:A\to\operatorname{Cont}(K,Z)$ has continuous evaluation $g^\flat:A\times K\to Z$, $g^\flat(a,k)=g(a)(k)$. These operations are mutually inverse and natural in $A$ and $Z$. Here compact means quasi-compact in the topological-space sense of [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], applied to the subspace topology on each subset.
